title: Google Analytics 4 (GA4) Event Architecture & Attribution
overview: Google Analytics 4 provides an event-based measurement model tracking user interactions across web and mobile platforms with machine-learning attribution modeling.
coreConcepts: Event-based data model replacing Universal Analytics session-based model
Data-Driven Attribution (DDA) modeling assigning fractional credit
Google Signals for cross-device reporting and demographic data
Measurement Protocol for server-side offline conversion ingestion
features: Automatic collection of enhanced measurement events (scrolls, outbound clicks, search)
Custom dimensions and user properties up to 50 scoped variables
BigQuery raw event export with daily and streaming tables
Predictive audiences for churn risk and purchase probability
bestPractices: Always mark primary business goals (purchase, generate_lead) as Key Events (formerly Conversions)
Link GA4 directly with Google Ads to import conversion actions and audiences
Configure custom data retention to 14 months (default is 2 months)
Pass standardized e-commerce items array with item_id, item_name, price, and currency
policies: Strict prohibition against transmitting Personally Identifiable Information (PII)
Compliance with European Data Protection DMA and ePrivacy directive
Google Analytics IP anonymization is permanently enabled by default
limitations: Standard property event processing latency: 24 to 48 hours for standard reports
Maximum 30 conversion events per standard property
Data thresholding applied when Google Signals is enabled and traffic volume is low
commonIssues: High volume of '(not set)' source/medium values due to broken UTM parameters
Discrepancies between GA4 purchase count and backend e-commerce orders
Data thresholding hiding custom dimension breakdowns

troubleshootingGuide.issue: Purchases undercounted compared to backend CRM
troubleshootingGuide.resolution: Deploy Measurement Protocol server-side webhook to capture users with aggressive adblockers

troubleshootingGuide.issue: UTM campaign traffic falling into 'Unassigned' default channel group
troubleshootingGuide.resolution: Ensure utm_source, utm_medium, and utm_campaign follow Google's standardized naming conventions
